steps: Start at the top line.
Curve to the left, down around the bottom line, and back up to close a tall oval.
countIdeas: Show an empty plate and say "zero cookies"
Take all the blocks out of a box and count what is left: zero
Ask how many elephants are in the room, then write 0
tip: Zero is taller and thinner than the letter O, so keep the oval narrow. Kids often skip zero when counting, so practice it as "none" with an empty cup or plate.
metaDescription: Free number 0 tracing worksheet. Trace a tall zero oval and teach "none" with an empty plate or cup. Printable practice for preschool and K.

steps: Start just below the top line and make a small slant up to the top.
Without lifting, pull a straight line down to the bottom line.
countIdeas: Put 1 spoon on the table
Find 1 red crayon in the box
Hop on 1 foot and count it out loud
tip: The little flag at the top is what keeps 1 from looking like a lowercase l. Once a child can pull a straight line down, 1 is a quick early win.
metaDescription: Print a free number 1 tracing worksheet. A small flag and one straight line down, plus easy counting ideas with spoons and crayons.

steps: Start on the left, just below the top line, and curve up and over to the right.
Without lifting, slant down to the left to the bottom line.
Finish with a straight line across the bottom line to the right.
countIdeas: Pair 2 socks from the laundry
Count 2 shoes by the door
Stack 2 blocks into a tower
tip: Children often reverse 2 so the hook faces left. A cue that works: "around the top like a hook, slide down, and walk across the floor."
metaDescription: Free number 2 tracing worksheet with a simple hook, slant, and line steps. Count pairs of socks and shoes too. Print and trace today.

steps: Start on the left, just below the top line, and curve around to the right and back in to the middle dashed line.
Without lifting, curve around to the right again and finish on the left near the bottom line.
countIdeas: Count 3 buttons into a cup
Line up 3 toy cars
Clap 3 times and count each clap
tip: A backward 3 looks like the letter E with round edges, and it is very common. Both bumps face right, so try "around the tree, around the tree" as you trace.
metaDescription: Print a free number 3 tracing worksheet that helps fix a backward 3. Two bumps facing right, with button and toy car counting ideas.

steps: Start at the top line and slant down to the left, stopping just below the middle dashed line.
Slide straight across to the right.
Lift your pencil, go back to the top, and pull the tall line straight down to the bottom line.
countIdeas: Count the 4 legs on a chair
Put 4 apples in a bowl
Find 4 wheels on a toy truck
tip: Four is made in two strokes: the slanted corner first, then the tall line from the top. Starting at the top every time keeps 4 from turning into a backward h.
metaDescription: Free number 4 tracing worksheet with simple two-stroke steps. Count chair legs, apples, and toy wheels to practice four. Printable for home or class.

steps: Start at the top line on the right and make a line across to the left.
Without lifting, pull down to just above the middle dashed line.
Curve out around to the right and down to the bottom line, ending on the left.
countIdeas: Count 5 fingers on one hand
Drop 5 pennies into a jar
Count 5 steps up the stairs
tip: Our 5 starts with the flat hat at the top, then goes down and around for the belly. If the belly faces left, it becomes a backward 5, so trace the curve slowly.
metaDescription: Print a free number 5 tracing worksheet. Hat first, then the round belly. Count 5 fingers, pennies, and steps for real-world practice.

steps: Start just below the top line on the right and curve down to the left.
Lift your pencil and make a circle at the bottom, starting on the left and curving down, between the middle dashed line and the bottom line.
countIdeas: Count 6 eggs in half a carton
Line up 6 crackers on a plate
Roll a die and find the 6 dots
tip: 6 and 9 are easy to mix up because one is the other turned upside down. 6 has its circle at the bottom, like a ball rolling down a slide.
metaDescription: Free number 6 tracing worksheet with clear steps to avoid 6 and 9 mix-ups. Count eggs and crackers to practice six. Ready to print.

steps: Make a line across the top line from left to right.
Without lifting, make a long slant down to the left to the bottom line.
countIdeas: Name the 7 days of the week
Count 7 crayons back into the box
Put 7 stickers on a page
tip: 7 is just two lines in one stroke, but kids sometimes flip it so the slant goes right. Remind them: across first, then slant back toward where you started.
metaDescription: Print a free number 7 tracing worksheet. Across and slant in one stroke, plus counting ideas like the 7 days of the week.

steps: Start at the middle dashed line and make a small circle on top, going up the right side first.
Make a bigger circle on the bottom, starting at the middle and curving down the left side.
countIdeas: Count the 8 legs on a toy spider
Count 8 grapes for snack
Stack 8 blocks and count as you build
tip: Our 8 is two circles, a small one on top and a bigger one underneath, like a snowman. Kids who struggle with the crossing figure-eight motion often find this way much easier.
metaDescription: Free number 8 tracing worksheet using two stacked circles like a snowman. Count spider legs and grapes to practice eight. Print it now.

steps: Start on the right, halfway between the top line and the middle dashed line, and curve up and around to the left to make a small circle.
Pull a straight line down the right side of the circle to the bottom line.
countIdeas: Count 9 pasta pieces onto a plate
Set up 9 bowling pins from a toy set
Count 9 beads onto a string
tip: 9 is a circle with a line, like a lowercase a with a taller stick. Its circle sits at the top, which is the easiest way to tell it apart from 6.
metaDescription: Print a free number 9 tracing worksheet. Circle on top, line down the side, with tips for 6 and 9 confusion and fun counting ideas.
